findings.recommendation: The domain class only accepts ASCII, so `logInfo("signup", { email: "ada@exämple.org" })` finds no match and writes the whole address to the logs kept 90 days by the hosting provider (GDPR Art. 5(1)(c), Art. 32), against the proposal's "masks every e-mail address". A non-ASCII local part leaks its prefix too (`jörg@example.de` becomes `jö` + `r***@example.de`). Match Unicode letters (`\p{L}`/`\p{N}` with the `u` flag) in the local part and the domain, and add a test for an internationalised address.
findings.title: Addresses with a non-ASCII domain are logged in full

findings.recommendation: The pattern requires a literal `@`, so a logged request path or query string such as `logInfo("GET /reset?email=ada%40example.org")` keeps the full address in the logs (GDPR Art. 5(1)(c)). Also match the percent-encoded separator (`%40`, case-insensitive) — or decode before masking — and add a test with an encoded address.
findings.title: URL-encoded addresses pass through unmasked
